message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules (Standard Edition)** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round when a player goes “Out.” | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck: 0–9, Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, Wild Draw Four.
• Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). On your turn you may:
1. **Play** one or more cards from your hand that match the top discard by **color**, **number**, or **symbol**.
2. If you play a **Wild** or **Wild Draw Four**, declare the new color.
3. If you cannot play, **draw** one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction (acts like Skip if only two players).
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk being challenged.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to call UNO when required results in a penalty: the player who missed it must draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | A round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring & Game End** | Add the round’s points to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (commonly 500). | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on colors** – If you’re low on cards, try to keep a variety of colors so you can always play something. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – Save Wild Draw Fours for when you’re about to win or when you’re stuck with high‑value cards. 3. **Watch opponents’ “UNO” calls** – If they forget, you can challenge them (if you suspect they had a playable card). 4. **Plan for reversals** – In a 2‑player game, a Reverse acts like a Skip, so use it to skip your opponent’s turn. Enjoy playing Uno!
